_sources.discrepancies: NCSL classifies Wyoming as photo ID required. Wyoming passed HB 238 in 2022 strengthening ID requirements. Wyoming offers same-day voter registration at the polls. 2026-06-10 verification: August 18, 2026 primary CONFIRMED (third Tuesday in August; FVAP 2026 primary calendar current as of May 2026). Wyoming enacted sweeping election-law changes effective for 2026: the absentee window (request and in-person absentee at the county clerk) was cut from 45 to 28 days before the election and in-person absentee is NOT available on Election Day — early-voting windows corrected accordingly (primary July 21-Aug 17; general Oct 6-Nov 2). Party-affiliation rule verified: existing voters had to declare/change party by May 13, 2026 for the primary (2023 crossover-voting law); the file's old claim that voters could change party at the polls on primary day was removed as outdated. New registrants may still declare a party when registering, including at the polls.

earlyVoting.notes: Absentee in-person voting at county clerk offices begins 28 days before Election Day (July 21, 2026) and is not available on Election Day. The absentee window was shortened from 45 to 28 days by 2025 legislation — confirm hours with your county clerk: https://sos.wyo.gov/elections/countycontacts.aspx

Absentee in-person voting at county clerk offices begins 28 days before Election Day (October 6, 2026) and is not available on Election Day. Any registered voter may request an absentee ballot without providing a reason. Same-day voter registration available at the polls with valid photo ID and proof of Wyoming residency.

Wyoming offers absentee voting for any registered voter without requiring a reason. Absentee in-person voting is available at county clerk offices starting 28 days before Election Day (not on Election Day itself). No online voter registration — register by mail or in person at the county clerk's office.

votingRules.phonesAtPollsDetail: Wyoming law prohibits photographing marked ballots. Cell phones may generally be brought into polling places but must not be used to photograph the ballot or other voters. Contact your county clerk for local polling place rules.
additionalRules: Wyoming has a closed primary — only voters registered with a party may vote in that party's primary. Existing voters had to declare or change party affiliation by May 13, 2026 to vote in the August 18 primary; new registrants may declare a party when registering, including at the polls.
Same-day voter registration is available at the polls with valid photo ID and proof of Wyoming residency.
Wyoming does not offer online voter registration — register by mail or at your county clerk's office.
Any registered voter may request an absentee ballot without providing a reason (no-excuse absentee).
Photo ID required at polls as of 2022 (HB 238).

eligibility: Any registered Wyoming voter may request an absentee ballot without providing a reason (no-excuse absentee)
voteByMail.applicationDeadline: Must be received by the county clerk at least 1 day before the election
voteByMail.returnDeadline: Must be received by the county clerk by the time polls close on Election Day (7:00 p.m.)
voteByMail.returnDeadlinePlain: Must arrive at the county clerk by 7 p.m. on Election Day. Postmarks do not count — ballot must be received.

primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEn: Wyoming has a closed primary (Wyo. Stat. Ann. §22-5-101). Only voters registered with a political party may vote in that party's primary. Voters must declare or change their party affiliation at least 96 days before the primary. Voters registered as independent or unaffiliated may not participate.
primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEs: Wyoming tiene una primaria cerrada (Wyo. Stat. Ann. §22-5-101). Solo los votantes registrados en un partido político pueden votar en la primaria de ese partido. Los votantes deben declarar o cambiar su afiliación de partido al menos 96 días antes de la primaria. Los votantes registrados como independientes o sin afiliación no pueden participar.
